extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners and patent applicants/practitioners handling PCT national-stage (35 U.S.C. 371) applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examination and prosecution of U.S. national-stage applications (35 U.S.C. 371) arising from PCT international applications, covering benefit claims, unity of invention, handling of international documents, drawings, IDS, and continuation/bypass practice. Primarily directed to examiner procedure and applicant obligations during national-stage processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit claim requirements under 37 CFR 1.78(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 and 365(c) of a prior-filed copending nonprovisional application or prior-filed copending international application designating the United States, the national stage application must comply with the requirements set forth in 37 CFR 1.78(d). The prior application must name as an inventor at least one inventor named in the later-filed international application and disclose the named inventor’s invention claimed in at least one claim of the national stage application in the manner provided by the first paragraph of 35 U.S.C. 112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The national stage application must contain a reference to the prior nonprovisional or international application identifying it by application number (series code and serial number) or international application number and international filing date and indicating the relationship of the applications. If international filing date is prior to Sept 16, 2012, the reference must be in either an application data sheet (37 CFR 1.76) or in the first sentence(s) of the specification; if on or after Sept 16, 2012, the reference must be in an application data sheet. Presentation of the benefit claim in the PCT Request form or presence on the front page of the published international application may satisfy ADS requirement in certain circumstances (see 37 CFR 1.76(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and non-extendable period for submitting benefit reference (37 CFR 1.78(d)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The required reference to the earlier filed application must be submitted within the time period set forth in 37 CFR 1.78(d)(3). This time period is not extendable and failure to timely submit the required reference will be considered a waiver of any benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, or 365(c) to such prior-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the entire delay between the due date under 37 CFR 1.78(d)(3) and the date the claim was filed was unintentional, a petition under 37 CFR 1.78(e) may be filed to accept the delayed claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on claiming benefit to the same international application in a national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371
rubrics_metrics.description: A national stage application submitted under 35 U.S.C. 371 may not claim benefit of the filing date of the international application of which it is the national stage, since its filing date is the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated differently: because the international application is not an earlier application (it has the same filing date as the national stage), a benefit claim under 35 U.S.C. 120 in the national stage to the international application is inappropriate. See also MPEP § 1893.03(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention requirement (37 CFR 1.475 / 37 CFR 1.499)
rubrics_metrics.description: A national stage application shall relate to one invention only or to a group of inventions so linked as to form a single general inventive concept (requirement of unity of invention). A group of inventions is considered linked where there is a technical relationship among the inventions involving at least one common or corresponding special technical feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The expression 'special technical features' means those technical features that define the contribution which each claimed invention, considered as a whole, makes over the prior art. The determination is made without regard to whether inventions are claimed separately or as alternatives within a single claim. See MPEP § 1850 for detailed discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and examples of 'special technical feature' and 'technical relationship'
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'special technical feature' defines the contribution which each claimed invention makes over the prior art. A 'technical relationship' among inventions involves at least one common or corresponding special technical feature linking them into a single general inventive concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a key defined by certain structural characteristics corresponding to claimed features of a lock; a process 'specially adapted' inherently produces the claimed product; an apparatus 'specifically designed' is suitable for carrying out a claimed process. 'Specially adapted' and 'specifically designed' do not imply exclusivity (i.e., product could be made by other processes or apparatus could be used for other processes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner obligations when making lack of unity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When making a lack of unity requirement the examiner must (1) list the different groups of claims and (2) explain why each group lacks unity with each other group, specifically describing the unique special technical feature in each group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a requirement may be made before any action on the merits and at any time before final action at examiner's discretion. Review is provided under 37 CFR 1.143 and 1.144. The examiner may make a lack of unity requirement in a national stage application even if no such requirement was made by the ISA or IPEA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted combinations when claims are to multiple categories of inventions (37 CFR 1.475(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A national stage application containing claims to different categories of invention will be considered to have unity of invention if the claims are drawn only to one of specified combinations of categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted combinations: (1) a product and a process specially adapted for the manufacture of said product; (2) a product and a process of use of said product; (3) a product, a process specially adapted for the manufacture of said product, and a use of said product; (4) a process and an apparatus or means specifically designed for carrying out the said process; (5) a product, a process specially adapted for manufacture of the said product, and an apparatus or means specifically designed for carrying out the said process. Otherwise unity might not be present (see 37 CFR 1.475(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction practice, election and applicable MPEP sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction practice in accordance with 37 CFR 1.141-1.146 continues to apply to U.S. national applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a), even if such an application claims benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 and 365(c) to an earlier international application or national stage application. Sections relating to double patenting, election and reply, and rejoinder generally also apply to national stage applications submitted under 35 U.S.C. 371.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 804 (double patenting rejections), 818 (election and reply), 821.04 (rejoinder of non-elected inventions), and 823 for related practice. Review of a lack of unity requirement is provided under 37 CFR 1.143 and 1.144; see 37 CFR 1.499 and MPEP § 1002.02(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejoinder criteria for nonelected claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner requires election and all claims drawn to the elected invention are allowable, the nonelected invention(s) should be considered for rejoinder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any nonelected product claim that requires all the limitations of an allowable product claim, and any nonelected process claim that requires all the limitations of an allowable process claim, should be rejoined. Nonelected processes of making/using an allowable product should be considered for rejoinder. Withdrawn process claims not commensurate in scope with an allowable product/apparatus claim will not be rejoined. Applicant is advised to amend process claims to require the limitations of the product/apparatus claim to preserve rejoinder. Rejoined claims must meet 35 U.S.C. 101, 102, 103 and 112; until all elected product/apparatus claims are found allowable, a restriction between product/apparatus and process claims may be maintained. Note prohibition against double patenting rejections of 35 U.S.C. 121 does not apply where restriction is withdrawn by examiner before patent issues (see MPEP § 804.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph and procedural headings for lack of unity actions in national-stage applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When beginning Lack of Unity actions in national stage applications submitted under 35 U.S.C. 371, examiners should begin with the specified heading and follow with appropriate form paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with heading (form paragraph 18.18) 'REQUIREMENT FOR UNITY OF INVENTION'; follow with form paragraph 18.19 or 18.20 as appropriate. For lack of unity during the international phase use form paragraph 18.05. Specific guidance exists for which subsequent form paragraphs to include (e.g., 18.06-18.07.02, 8.21.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction requirement and use of form paragraph 18.19
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction is required under 35 U.S.C. 121 and 372. Form paragraph 18.19 is used to require applicant to elect a single invention to which the claims must be restricted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using this paragraph, follow with form paragraphs 18.06 - 18.06.02 and 18.07 - 18.07.02 as appropriate. Notify applicant that if product/apparatus claims are allowable, certain process claims may be considered for rejoinder by using form paragraph 8.21.04. Reconsider propriety of restriction when elected invention claims are in condition for allowance to verify non-elected claims do not share same or corresponding technical feature with allowable claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of species (form paragraph 18.20) and content of election replies
rubrics_metrics.description: When application contains claims to more than one species of the generic invention, species are deemed to lack unity; applicant is required to elect a single species to which the claims shall be restricted if no generic claim is finally held allowable. Reply must identify claims readable on the elected species; argument that a claim is allowable or all claims are generic is non-responsive unless accompanied by an election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon allowance of a generic claim, applicant entitled to consideration of claims to additional species written in dependent form or otherwise requiring all limitations of an allowed generic claim. Form paragraph usage instructions include identifying species in bracket 1 and generic claims in bracket 2 or NONE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election by original presentation and traversal requirements (form paragraph 18.21 & 18.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: An election can be made by original presentation; newly submitted claims directed to invention that lacks unity with originally claimed invention may be treated as constructively elected by original presentation. To preserve right to petition, reply must distinctly and specifically point out supposed errors in the restriction requirement (traverse).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Traversal must be timely; failure to timely traverse results in loss of right to petition under 37 CFR 1.144. If applicant traverses on grounds that inventions are not patentably distinct, applicant should submit evidence or identify evidence now of record showing inventions are obvious variants, or clearly admit such on the record; such evidence or admission may be used in a 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection of the other invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for election replies to be complete
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply to a restriction/election requirement must include (i) an election of a species or invention to be examined even though the requirement may be traversed and (ii) identification of the claims encompassing the elected invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Election may be with or without traverse; to preserve petition right election must be made with traverse and traversal must be presented at time of election to be timely. If claims are added after election, applicant must indicate which claims are readable on the elected invention/species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents communicated by the International Bureau included in national-stage file
rubrics_metrics.description: The national stage application includes documents communicated by the International Bureau and submissions from applicant. Important items include (A) cover page with applicant/inventor data, application data and abstract, (B) description, claims and drawings, and (C) the search report (Form PCT/ISA/210) if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cover page is important for correct application data (filing date, priority date). If international application published in English, the Office uses the description, claims, abstract and drawings as published for the U.S. national stage application. The description/claims/drawings reflect application subject matter on the international filing date and are important for comparison to amendments to check for new matter. The search report reflects the ISA's opinion regarding prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract reproduction rule for national-stage filing receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract is reproduced on the cover page of the publication and the requirement of 37 CFR 1.52(b) that the abstract commence on a separate sheet does not apply to the copy communicated to designated Offices under PCT Article 20.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is improper for the examiner to require applicant to provide an abstract commencing on a separate sheet if the abstract does not appear on a separate sheet in the publication of the international application. Unless properly amended under U.S. rules during national-stage processing, the abstract on the cover page of the published international application will be the abstract published by the USPTO under 35 U.S.C. 122(b) and in any U.S. patent issuing from the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of IPER/IPRP (international preliminary examination/report on patentability)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an international preliminary examination is performed, an IPER (Form PCT/IPEA/409) is prepared and sent to elected Offices; it reflects the IPEA's non-binding opinion regarding lack of unity, novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability. If no timely demand for international preliminary examination, an IPRP (Chapter I) reflecting the ISA's non-binding opinion is sent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may adopt any portion or all of the report upon consideration in the national stage so long as consistent with U.S. practice. The first Office action on the merits should indicate the report has been considered (even a mere acknowledgement). IPER may include annexes (amendments) and indicate which pages were basis of report; review IPER as roadmap for what happened during Chapter II examination to determine which version to examine. If IPER was in a foreign language, IB will translate IPER but will not translate annexes; foreign-language annexes not timely translated by applicant will be considered canceled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking and treatment of replacement/amended sheets from international phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Replacement sheets and amendments made under PCT Article 19 or 34 and other modifications are marked to indicate their type and date and are listed in the IPER as 'originally filed/furnished' or as amended sheets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement sheets showing format-only changes are marked 'SUBSTITUTE SHEET'; rectifications of obvious error accepted by ISA/IPEA are marked 'RECTIFIED SHEET (RULE 91)'; sheets incorporated by reference marked 'INCORPORATED BY REFERENCE (RULE 20.6)'; Article 19 amended claim sheets marked 'AMENDED SHEET (Article 19)'; Article 34 amendments marked 'AMENDED SHEET'. IPER Box No. I indicates claim numbers considered and dates received. The NOTICE OF ACCEPTANCE OF APPLICATION UNDER 35 U.S.C. 371 (Form PCT/DO/EO/903) should be consulted to see if annexes or translations were entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of withdrawal and effect on national-stage entry
rubrics_metrics.description: If national-stage papers include an indication that the international application or US designation has been withdrawn, the file should be brought to the attention of International Patent Legal Administration to determine whether withdrawal occurred prior to completion of requirements under 35 U.S.C. 371(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If withdrawal occurred prior to completion of 371(c), then entry into the U.S. national stage is prohibited (see 35 U.S.C. 366). The indication of withdrawal may appear on various IB/RO forms (PCT/IB/307, PCT/RO/136, PCT/RO/117, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Title of the invention for official filing receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: In absence of an application data sheet (37 CFR 1.76) or preliminary amendment changing the title, the Office will use the title that appears on the first page of the description of the published international application (or the English translation) in preparing the official filing receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the title does not appear on the first page of the description and no ADS or preliminary amendment changing the title has been furnished, the title will be taken from the cover page. If applicant furnishes both an ADS and a preliminary amendment, the later-filed document governs; an ADS will govern over a concurrently filed preliminary amendment. See 37 CFR 1.76(d)(1)-(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings and PCT Rule 11 limitations in national-stage examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO may not impose drawing requirements during examination of a national-stage application beyond those imposed by the PCT (e.g., PCT Rule 11).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may require new drawings if the drawings were published without meeting all PCT requirements for drawings. Applicant may file amended drawings under 37 CFR 1.84 and 1.121(d) during national stage, including replacing black-and-white with color drawings with a grantable petition and fee. If an international application filed with color drawings was published with only black-and-white drawings, applicant is entitled to rely on color drawings present on the international filing date to determine whether later amendments seeking to add color drawings include new matter. Guidance on petitions to accept color drawings provided in MPEP § 608.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Disclosure Statement (IDS) duty in national-stage applications (37 CFR 1.56 / 1.63)
rubrics_metrics.description: The duty to disclose information material to patentability as defined in 37 CFR 1.56 is placed on individuals associated with filing and prosecution of a national-stage application in the same manner as for a domestic application. The averment required under 37 CFR 1.63(b)(3) in an oath or declaration is applicable to oaths/declarations filed in U.S. national-stage applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When requirements for a national-stage application have been completed, applicant is notified (Form PCT/DO/EO/903) including whether a copy of the international search report and copies of the references cited are present in the national-stage file. The examiner will consider documents cited in the international search report (and copies of the documents) when both the international search report (or supplementary ISR under PCT Rule 45bis) and copies are indicated to be present in the national stage file, without further action by applicant under 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98. The examiner will note consideration in the first Office action. There is no requirement that examiners list the documents on a PTO-892 form; otherwise applicant must follow 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 to ensure examiner considers documents cited in the international search report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation of automatic consideration of international-cited documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice of automatically considering documents applies only to documents cited in the international search report relative to a national-stage application filed under 35 U.S.C. 371.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It does not apply to documents cited in an international preliminary examination report that are not cited in the search report, nor to applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) claiming the benefit of an international application filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation, divisional, and continuation-in-part ('bypass') applications of a PCT application
rubrics_metrics.description: It is possible to file a U.S. national application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) during the pendency of an international application designating the United States without completing the requirements for entering the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371(c). Such continuing applications filed during pendency of the international application are often referred to as 'bypass' applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 and 365(c) of a prior international application designating the U.S., the continuing application must: (A) include a specific reference to the prior international application; (B) be copending with the prior international application; and (C) have at least one inventor in common with the prior international application. Continuation-in-part applications are generally filed where applicants seek to add matter not supported by the international application as originally filed; new matter may not be added to a U.S. national-stage application (see 37 CFR 1.121(f)).
